messages.subject: Ecological Research Assistant: Quantitative Ecology – Mathematical/Statistical Modeling, R programming, Data Analysis
parts:
USGS PATUXENT WILDLIFE RESEARCH CENTER

The USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center is searching for an
extremely motivated and talented research assistant to work about 20
hours per week for approx 12 months beginning as early as June 2013.

The position involves data analysis, estimation, and modeling in
support of various projects focused on population, metapopulation,
community ecology, spatial sampling of animal populations, spatial
ecology, and wildlife surveys. The incumbent will analyze capture-
recapture data, develop statistical software in the R programming
environment, and work on data analysis and GIS in support of the North
American Amphibian Monitoring Program (NAAMP). Knowledge of the R
programming environment is required. Must be highly motivated and able
to work independently. Other desired skills include knowledge of
likelihood and Bayesian methods of statistical inference, Markov chain
Monte Carlo, especially implementation in WinBUGS, and GIS. Other
duties as assigned.

The ideal candidate has a degree in Ecology, Natural Resources,
Statistics, is currently enrolled in a graduate program, and is
interested in the application of quantitative methods to ecological
problems as an element of his or her graduate research.

Students are responsible for all costs of transportation to and from
Patuxent Wildlife Research Center. Salary depends on qualifications
(Hourly rates - BS degree: $17.56; BS plus 1 year experience: $21.75;
MS degree $26.61). Successful applicant becomes a Student Contractor.
Applicants must be: 1) enrolled in a degree-seeking program, or 2)
recent graduate, less than 1-year since graduation date.

Principal Duty Station:
USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center
12100 Beech Forest Road
Laurel, Maryland 20708-4038

To apply, send the following to Andy Royle at the above address or via
email (aro...@usgs.gov) or FAX (301.497.5545):

1) Letter of interest, professional interests, and career goals (if
any).
2) Piece of R code that does something interesting, useful,
efficiently, or in a novel way. (also describe what it does, just in
case).
3) Resume, including relevant experience, list of relevant classes,
contact information and two or three reference contacts
